shared_elements: low-relief carving on a stone slab/pillar face
clustered motifs filling the upper part of the surface
justification: Both surfaces carry shallow, rounded low relief on unpolished stone in which discs/circles and curving snake-like bands are the most legible motifs, and both concentrate a cluster of arch- or bag-like rounded forms toward the upper edge. However, B is organised into clear horizontal registers separated by a patterned band and contains unambiguous animal figures (quadrupeds, a long-necked bird), while A is a close-up of an unregistered, largely non-figurative jumble of circles and loops, so the compositional logic differs sharply.
